topic: The Ever Given and the Suez Canal, March 2021 (30-second sample)
method: Primary agency pages (ESA, NASA) read directly; shipping press and reference summaries via web search, cross-checked; estimates kept as estimates and attributed.

claims.claim: The container ship Ever Given ran aground in the Suez Canal on 23 March 2021 and was refloated on 29 March 2021, about six days later.

sources.title: ESA: Suez Canal traffic jam seen from space (Copernicus Sentinel-1, March 2021)
sources.quote: The giant container ship ran aground in the canal on 23 March; the image on the right, captured on 25 March, shows the 400 m-ship blocking the canal

sources.title: Seatrade Maritime: Ever Given blocking Suez Canal re-floated

claims.notes: Partial refloat early on 29 March, full refloat about 15:05 local time (SCA).

claims.claim: The Ever Given is 400 metres long, longer than the Eiffel Tower is tall (330 m). It can carry about 20,000 twenty-foot containers (TEU).

sources.title: ESA: Suez Canal traffic jam seen from space (Copernicus Sentinel-1, March 2021)
Riviera Maritime Media: Evergreen box ship blocks Suez Canal
Seatrade Maritime / Khaleej Times: the Ever Given carries the equivalent of 20,000 twenty-foot containers
sources.quote: [search summary] it carries the equivalent of 20,000 units of 20-foot containers

claims.notes: Comparison stands the ship on end: a scale picture, not an event.

claims.claim: The Ever Given was sailing from China to the Netherlands.

sources.title: ESA: Suez Canal traffic jam seen from space (Copernicus Sentinel-1, March 2021)
sources.quote: on its journey from China to the Netherlands

sources.title: 2021 Suez Canal obstruction (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: bound from Tanjung Pelepas/Yantian (China) to Rotterdam

claims.notes: Map uses Shanghai as a stand-in Chinese port; Rotterdam was the destination. The on-screen route is labelled as the route, not the exact track.

claims.claim: By 28 March 2021 at least 369 ships were reported queuing to pass through the canal.

sources.title: 2021 Suez Canal obstruction (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: On 28 March, at least 369 ships were queuing to pass through the canal

sources.title: Port Economics, Management and Policy: Blockage of the Suez Canal, March 2021
sources.quote: [search summary] by 28 March, at least 369 ships were queuing

claims.notes: Counts came from the canal authority and shipping agents and changed daily; attributed as reported.

claims.claim: Lloyd's List estimated that the blockage held up about 9.6 billion US dollars of goods a day (its own rough calculation; figures of 9.5-9.7 billion appear in different reports). Lloyd's List split it as about 5.1 billion westbound and 4.5 billion eastbound.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Suez Canal blockage halts $9.6bn a day of ship traffic (25 March 2021)
sources.quote: [search summary] $9.6bn a day, citing Lloyd's List

sources.title: Engineering News / Bloomberg: Suez snarl seen halting $9.6bn a day worth of ship traffic

contradictions: Some reports give 9.5 or 9.7 billion; Lloyd's List called its numbers rough calculations.
claims.notes: Shown with an ESTIMATE badge and named source.

claims.claim: Sailing from Tokyo to Rotterdam round the southern tip of Africa instead of through the canal adds about 3,300 nautical miles (3,315 by the World Economic Forum's figure).

sources.title: World Economic Forum: The Suez Canal in numbers (March 2021)
sources.quote: 3,315 nautical miles: distance saving Tokyo-Rotterdam via the canal rather than the southern tip of Africa

sources.title: Windward: What is the Suez Canal
sources.quote: [search summary] detour adds approximately 3,500-4,000 nautical miles

contradictions: The extra distance depends on the ports: 3,000 to 5,000 nautical miles in other sources.

claims.claim: NASA's Terra satellite (ASTER) photographed more than 100 freighters waiting at the canal's southern entrance during the blockage.

sources.title: NASA/JPL Photojournal PIA24553: Suez Canal Crisis
sources.quote: the southern entrance to the Suez Canal, where over 100 freighters wait their turn

claims.claim: Tug boats and a high tide freed the ship on 29 March 2021. NASA reported the tide rose about 46 centimetres above normal that day.

sources.title: NASA Earth Observatory: Traffic Jam on the Suez Canal
sources.quote: the tides in the Suez Canal rose about 46 centimeters above normal on March 29

sources.title: NBC News: Suez Canal ship Ever Given partially refloated after huge effort

claims.claim: On 21 March 2021, before the grounding, Sentinel-1 radar showed routine traffic in the canal with vessels every 2 to 3 km.

sources.title: ESA: Suez Canal traffic jam seen from space
sources.quote: The image on the left, captured on 21 March, shows routine maritime traffic in the canal with vessels visible every 2 to 3 km.
